title: Add support to Get Log Page command and response
description:
The fist push adds the Get Log Page Command decode and responses for pages 0-5 and 0x70.
The rest of the patches add per-page decoding.

See screenshots:
Short Request:
![image](/uploads/fb2a3ba07715271fda58374b86d39ded/image.png)

Full Response:
![image](/uploads/30cf8d65e81ed8387d0c979b8fa54d50/image.png)

another approach could be to use the range_string type instead of this helper.

Pascal, thank you for your willingness to review this. I have removed the gcc-11 compile commit.

I see no problem viewing complete patches. Please press "toggle commit list" in the latest commit section and you will see commits one by one. Each commit can be browsed seprarately (cliked on the commit link). Gitalb java-script side may warn you on collapsing some sections, and may suggest to press "expand all files button". After this, all individual commits are seen.

Actually, I recommend reviewing commits one by one as it will make a logical sense. The first commit lays a foundation, each other commit adds a single page decoding.

I am willing to do about anything possible to make the review process more convinient for you. Please let me know if you have a request.
You marked this thread as resolved, but did not comment regarding the range_string approach. I wanted to know if you were aware of its existence.

Wrong thread marked as resolved, sorry.

I was not aware of range_string, looking it up.

OK, I have looked it up, and I liked it. It really answers my previous question to the review comments, when a core developer asked me to to change proto_item_append_text() to VALS() in field definitions.

I asked then -- "how do I print the "Reserved" string then and what would be the equivalent of val_to_str(val, table, "Reserved"). 

I have this answer now.

Since we have this a a repeated pattern now (spanning previous MRs), I am willing to do it as a separate MR, that will spawn the previous MRs.

Two questions:
1. Are you OK with separate MR?
2. Do you think such change is needed? (I am OK with it, but I do not insist.)

I'm perfectly fine with a separate MR.

I'm done for today so I will review your latest iteration hopefully tomorrow and merge it.
Would this be a candidate for FT_NONE type instead of FT_BYTES? Or is there an interest for filtering on the byte string?

Basically, what I am trying to do here (I assume you refer to printing the entire record here) is to have the record being displayed as a collapsible section, under which I have the individual decoding for all present fields. Thus, I would like the fields to be displayed in the context of the record, and the section to actually display the bytes it contains.

The complication we have with Get LogPage is the offset parameter, which makes the size not known beforehand. In addition I would like to print the record number. So, we have both the variable size, and the suffix to print. So, the easiest way to do it is with  proto_tree_add_bytes_format(), correct?

If I miss it, please let me know.
Ok that's fine.
Same comment as above

This is the same as above - I would like the section to display the bytes, and I would like to add the page name to the section. The reason I would like to show the bytes is two-fold:
1. We do not decode all pages yet.
2. Even for decoded pages, I would like to be able to see where the decoded fields are in the context of the response itself.

OK?
Yes.

If I'm not mistaken, there is an overlap with the hf_nvme_get_logpage_dword10 array (the former is 4 bytes long starting from offset 42 and the later is 4 bytes longs starting from offset 42). Is this expected?

Yes, this is correct. The lower 16 bit for number of dwords field are DWORD-10 (offset 42)  , the upper-16 bit are DWORD-11 (offset 44). So, while DWORD-10 and DWORD-11 are displayed and decoded separately, the entire value (that spans DWORD-10 and DWORD-11) is also shown.

I could have just added a line, but overlapped display makes it clearer where the bytes are.

![image](/uploads/dd535d50c059851658beff157be29fd5/image.png)

Hi Constantine,

besides the small comments (it seems like the FT_BYTES vs FT_NONE is used this way in the dissector, not sure it is worth a change - or would be more suited in another MR), I guess the current WIP could be merged. Let me know your thoughts regarding my remarks, and remove the WIP keyword if you want to merge the current state of the art.

I have a two or three pages left to decode (except for async event, which will be a separate MT anyway), but I am OK with pushing now, while you have time to review and the things are fresh in your memory.

I have found a missing filter suffix names for dword10 array that I am fixing, as well as a duplicate line for ANA. I am pushing those and removing the WIP line.

Again thanks.

Hi Constantine,

I compiled your patch series on a Windosw machine and MSVC still complains about stest_type_done_tbl not being const. I ended duplicating the value_string array as it seems less hacky and pleases MSVC. I hope this is OK with you.

Our pre-commit hook (that can be copied from tools/pre-commit to your .git/hook folder) also noticed that hf_nvme_get_logpage_pred_lat_etype entries are unused. Should we remove them? Or is there a typo somewhere?

It is a typo (not using the field). Shall be 
```
if (off <= 2 && (4 - off) <= len)
        add_group_mask_entry(cmd_tvb, grp, 2-off, 2, ASPEC(hf_nvme_get_logpage_pred_lat_etype));
```
I am correcting this now, as well as windows compile issue (by duplicating the arrays).

I have researched it further, and I see that there is a different behavior of
```
#define VALS(x)     (cast_same(const struct _value_string*, (x)))
```
on Windows and Unix platforms.

On Unix platforms, the required type for the pointer will be  `value_string * const`, and on Windows platform, I guess the required pointer type is `const value_string *`, and the difference cannot be reconciled on both platforms. 

My reading of this is that Windows compiler behaves correctly (albeit too strict not allowing to reconcile with `const value_string * const`), while gcc and CLANG follow the purpose of the definition, despite the fact that definition is probably not correct and should have been `(cast_same(struct _value_string* const, (x)))`.
@pquantin, thak you for testing the windows build for me. I have pushed both fixes.
